mode: facts only; no forecast, valuation, ranking, market-price inference or action

identity.question: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 50+ bps after the October 2026 meeting?

resolution_facts.meeting: FOMC scheduled October 27-28, 2026; statement is resolution source.
resolution_facts.measurement: Change in target federal funds range upper bound versus pre-October-meeting level; official range 3.75-4.00%, upper bound 4.00%.
resolution_facts.rounding: When changed level is not one displayed option, market says round the change up to nearest 25 bp; e.g. 12.5 bp increase counts as 25 bp.
resolution_facts.fallback: No statement by end of next scheduled meeting => No change.

latest_action.statement: Activity solid; job gains kept pace, unemployment little changed; inflation elevated.

sep_2026.interpretation_limit: Individual end-2026 appropriate-policy projections; not October decision forecast/probabilities.

official_economic_releases.facts: CPI-U +0.6% m/m SA, +3.7% y/y NSA; core +0.3% m/m, +2.6% y/y. Gasoline +9.1%, >half monthly all-items increase.
Final demand PPI +1.3% m/m SA, +6.3% y/y NSA.
PCE +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%; +3.4% y/y, core +3.0%. Sep PCE release Oct 29, after meeting.
Payrolls +29,000; unemployment 4.2%; hourly earnings +0.1% m/m, +3.0% y/y; Jul/Aug payroll revisions net -60,000. Oct report Nov 6.

signed_policy_communications.speaker: Governor Christopher J. Waller
signed_policy_communications.fact: Said if data continue as expected, he anticipates additional hikes; timing flexible, hikes need not be consecutive. Explicitly personal view, not necessarily colleagues/FOMC. No hike size assigned.

signed_policy_communications.speaker: Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson
signed_policy_communications.fact: Supported September +25 bp hike; described activity/labor as broadly solid and inflation above target; upside inflation risks from geopolitical developments and stronger-than-expected demand.
